title: Charlie Mack and Joe Gorham send the band to Chicago
summary: Charlie Mack, hearing the band on a wagon, leads to Joe Gorham booking them at the Grunewald Cave; the group goes to Chicago and the Lambs Cafe.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, about then, yeah. And, uh, so we were, we were, we were playing on this wagon up in Down Canal Street. Blasting away. It just went about five o'clock, you know. The fight starts at eight. And there's a couple of guys standing around and listening to us. And one said, one come over here. He says, say, buddy. He said, uh, y'all really plays that stuff. He was a white fellow. See, he talked just like an eagle. And who was it? But Charlie Mack of Swar and Mack. They were at the Orphium that week. The two black crows. Oh, yeah. So, he said, I'd let y'all go north. He said, oh, we're gonna give you. Sure, I said, oh, give me an Orphium. Yeah, we sure. I'll fix it. So, next thing I know, there's a fellow by the name of Joe Gorham. Had a girl by the name of Myrtle Howard, working at the Rosefell, at the Grumwald Hotel then.
Called the Cave, remember? And, uh, I don't know how old you are, but I imagine you remember those days, because it's been a long time since it's been called the Grumwald.
Um, I haven't lived there that long, but anyway, I remember some old books and pictures after it called that. Yeah, yeah. I remember seeing a lot of pictures.

Theodore Grumwald was the manager, see, the owner, rather. And, uh, so this Wyntle Howard, this beautiful review she had on it. And she was a beautiful dancer. So her manager, might have been her husband, I don't know, he come to me one day. He said he got a, when Sworn Mac went back to Chicago, they put the buzz on to Smiley Carbett. Smiley's going around crazy looking for a band. He had a little gypsy outfit. Uh, Drigo, the gypsy violinist, used to dance around there and smile at the women. You know, the guy, get out of here, you polack, you know. So, and the joint was dying, you know. So, Charlie Mac, he buzzed Smiley and so Smiley sends Joe to go and contact these guys. He said, alright. So Joe called me. He got a hold of us and he, he, he, he fell up a deal for us. And from there on we went. And, oh God. We went to the Lambs and stayed there, jam packed the joint. First we went out there, they want to run us out. Yeah, they didn't want no part of us. And, uh, so it so happened that this, a show called Made in America, it was a Schubert show. It was playing at the Palisade, right at the corner, across from the Lambs. Lambs on Clark Randolph, see.
So it was right in the loop then? In the loop, yeah, right in the loop. I always thought it was maybe up farther north on Clark, on the north side.
No, no, just right in the loop, right opposite the Hotel Sherman.
See. And, uh, and City Hall was on the other corner. Who?
The City Hall, the big City Hall, right there. Oh, the City Hall, another club. The City Hall, yeah, sure, that's right, right on.
